question: What are the five main pitfalls B2B marketers make when running LinkedIn ads campaigns?
transcript_excerpt: The five pitfalls are: using LinkedIn's default geographic targeting (recent instead of permanent location), leaving LinkedIn audience expansion checked by default, auto-selecting the LinkedIn audience network placement which wastes 95-98% of budget on bot or spam traffic, running campaigns on maximum delivery bidding which is the most expensive option, and using manual bidding without understanding proper bid ranges (most clients pay 7-9 dollars per landing page click, not 20+ dollars).

question: How does LinkedIn's Revenue Attribution Report (RAR) help B2B companies measure ad performance differently from Google and Meta?
transcript_excerpt: LinkedIn's Revenue Attribution Report integrates with CRMs like HubSpot, Salesforce, and Microsoft Dynamics to show when a deal reaches sales qualified lead status or closed deal status. It reveals which company employees interacted with your ads and company posts, proving your targeting is accurate and showing how multiple channels work together. This is unique because only LinkedIn knows where people work, whereas Google cannot build this report because they don't know what company someone works for.

question: What is the LIFAT ID on LinkedIn and why does it improve conversion tracking accuracy?
transcript_excerpt: The LIFAT ID is LinkedIn's unique identifier for each individual that gets inserted into the URL when someone clicks on an ad. When you capture and send this ID back to LinkedIn through your tech team as a first-party cookie, you achieve a 95% match rate instead of the 40-50% match rate from the Conversions API. This means you can reliably track 95% of conversions versus only 50-70% before using this parameter.

question: How do Thought Leadership Ads on LinkedIn outperform traditional company-sponsored ads in engagement and cost?
transcript_excerpt: Thought Leadership Ads sponsor an individual's post rather than a company's post. Testing shows that the same message from an individual has three times the engagement rate and one-third the cost compared to the same message from an unknown company. The highest performing ad format is a personal video of someone sharing a tip, trick, strategy, or industry update, then promoted through the ad account with retargeting to viewers who watched 50% or more of the video.

question: Why are B2B companies shifting budget from Google Ads to LinkedIn as of 2024?
transcript_excerpt: Google has been slowly chipping away at optimization capabilities by removing targeting and segmentation options, reaching a point where companies now believe it is no longer as useful. B2B companies are moving budget to LinkedIn because LinkedIn has improved its measurement capabilities with tools like the Revenue Attribution Report, giving advertisers proof that LinkedIn actually delivers quality results, whereas previously it was a crapshoot and a guess.

question: What is the recommended approach for implementing LinkedIn ads if you want to measure ROI effectively and scale efficiently?
transcript_excerpt: The recommendation is to nail efficiency at small scale first in a very controlled way so you understand what's happening, then scale from there. You can increase audience size, break audiences into smaller functional pieces called micro segments, or increase budget and bid to reach more of your audience. This approach makes it easy to identify what isn't working if something fails, rather than jumping in with a large budget and Frankensteining things together.
